title: Change or remove anything about a release
statement: As a developer, I can change or delete a release, its notes, its story links and the template, so the Saga holds the current truth rather than stale records.
overview: Git is the history: a release that should not exist is deleted. Whiteboards have no delete today because their revisions are immutable; archive is what exists, and this story does not change that.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Every release record has CLI commands to create, read, update and delete it: a release, a note, a story link, a checklist step, a template step and the versioning scheme.
Deleting a release removes its notes, steps and story links and changes no story; `--dry-run` reports the same effect and writes nothing.
A release's version can be corrected by an explicit command, and is refused if another release has that version.
The process overview is changed with the existing `whiteboard publish`, `rename` and `archive` commands.
